DOM TOL - Pre-Procedure History & Physical
Salient Features
Clinical Profile


75-year-old man with severe multivessel coronary artery disease, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia.


Continues to experience an exertional anginal equivalent characterized by arm discomfort with exercise lasting approximately 5-15 minutes and resolving within 2-5 minutes of rest.


Diagnostic coronary angiography on 05/20/2026 demonstrated severe multivessel CAD:


LAD: long segment of diffuse sequential approximately 70% disease involving the proximal LAD across the first diagonal segment.


First diagonal: approximately 85-90% stenosis beyond the ostium.


LCx: multiple sequential mid-to-distal lesions up to approximately 60-70%.


RCA: diffuse disease with approximately 50% ostial/proximal disease and distal subtotal occlusion, with robust left-to-right collateralization.




Previous coronary CTA demonstrated severe LAD and multifocal RCA disease with coronary calcium score of 446.


Stress echocardiography demonstrated exertional left arm pain, 1.5-2.0 mm ST-T changes, questionable distal septal hypokinesis, and Duke treadmill score -7.


Revascularization options, including CABG versus complex multivessel PCI, were previously reviewed. Patient expressed preference for PCI if technically feasible.


Current plan is angioplasty and stent placement of the right coronary artery on 10/08/2026. 


Procedure


Planned coronary angiography with PCI/angioplasty and stent placement of the right coronary artery.


Target lesion: severely diseased/subtotally occluded RCA.


Procedure scheduled for 10/08/2026.


Patient remains on aspirin, clopidogrel, beta-blocker, and antianginal therapy per the available medication record.


Disposition


Proceed with planned RCA angioplasty/stent intervention.


Follow up with Dr. Singh approximately one week following the procedure.


Procedure Summary
Domingo Tolentino is a 75-year-old man undergoing pre-procedure evaluation prior to planned coronary angiography with PCI of the right coronary artery. He has diabetes mellitus and severe multivessel coronary artery disease documented by prior coronary CTA, abnormal stress testing, and invasive coronary angiography.
Cardiac catheterization on 05/20/2026 demonstrated severe multivessel disease involving the LAD, diagonal branch, circumflex, and RCA. The RCA was diffusely diseased with ostial/proximal disease and distal subtotal occlusion with collateral filling. The LAD demonstrated diffuse sequential approximately 70% stenoses, with 85-90% disease of the first diagonal branch. The circumflex contained sequential lesions of approximately 60-70%.
He continues to describe exertional arm discomfort that resolves with rest, consistent with his previously documented exertional anginal symptoms. After prior discussion of CABG versus complex multivessel PCI, the current treatment plan is angioplasty and stent placement of the right coronary artery on 10/08/2026. 
Detailed Procedure
The patient's cardiovascular history and prior coronary studies were reviewed in preparation for planned coronary intervention.
Coronary CT angiography from 12/11/2025 demonstrated severe mid-LAD disease, moderate first diagonal disease, and severe multifocal RCA stenosis, with a coronary calcium score of 446.
Stress echocardiography from 11/18/2025 demonstrated preserved LV systolic function with LVEF 55-60%. Exercise was terminated because of left arm pain, which increased to 5/10 at peak exercise. The exercise ECG demonstrated 1.5-2.0 mm ST-T changes, with questionable distal septal hypokinesis on stress imaging. Duke treadmill score was -7.
Subsequent invasive coronary angiography on 05/20/2026 demonstrated a patent left main without significant obstructive disease. The LAD was moderately calcified with a long segment of severe disease consisting of sequential approximately 70% stenoses involving the proximal LAD and extending across the first diagonal segment. The first diagonal branch demonstrated 85-90% stenosis. The mid-to-distal circumflex contained multiple sequential lesions up to approximately 60-70%.
The RCA was diffusely diseased with approximately 50% ostial stenosis, a long proximal segment of approximately 50% disease, and distal subtotal occlusion with robust left-to-right collateralization and favorable distal targets.
Given diabetes mellitus, complex multivessel CAD, and symptomatic exertional angina, CABG versus multivessel PCI was previously discussed. The patient expressed preference for PCI if technically feasible while remaining willing to consider CABG if clinically indicated. Medical therapy was intensified with aspirin, clopidogrel, beta-blocker, statin, and antianginal therapy.
The current treatment plan documents angioplasty and stent placement of the right coronary artery on 10/08/2026. 
Impression


Severe multivessel coronary artery disease. (ICD-10: I25.10)


Distal subtotal occlusion/severe disease of the right coronary artery.


Severe diffuse LAD disease with sequential approximately 70% stenoses.


Severe first diagonal stenosis, approximately 85-90%.


Diffuse circumflex disease with sequential approximately 60-70% lesions.


Exertional anginal equivalent manifested by arm discomfort relieved with rest.


Abnormal stress testing with exercise-induced ST-T changes and left arm pain.


Type 2 diabetes mellitus. (ICD-10: E11.9)


Essential hypertension. (ICD-10: I10)


Hyperlipidemia. (ICD-10: E78.5)


Planned coronary angiography with RCA angioplasty and stent placement.

ROB MOR - Pre-Procedure History & Physical
Salient Features
Clinical Profile


68-year-old man with coronary artery disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity, and former tobacco use.


Currently reports feeling well and denies chest pain, shortness of breath, unusual fatigue, or persistent peripheral edema.


Prior coronary CT angiographic evaluation demonstrated a markedly elevated coronary calcium score of approximately 992, reported at the 83rd percentile for age.


Stress echocardiogram 08/19/2026 demonstrated preserved LV systolic function with LVEF 55-60%.


Exercised 5 minutes 27 seconds on standard Bruce protocol, achieving 97% of predicted maximal heart rate.


Exercise ECG demonstrated 1-1.5 mm ST-T wave changes, although there was no 2D echocardiographic evidence of inducible ischemia at the achieved workload.


Duke treadmill score was 0, moderate risk for CAD.


Given the markedly elevated coronary calcium burden, abnormal exercise ECG response, diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity, and overall elevated coronary risk profile, invasive coronary angiography was recommended for definitive assessment of coronary anatomy.


Diagnostic coronary angiography is scheduled at St. John's on 10/07/2026. 


Procedure


Planned diagnostic coronary angiography for definitive evaluation of coronary anatomy.


Planned wrist/radial access per the documented procedural discussion.


Same-day discharge anticipated if there are no procedural complications.


Disposition


Proceed with scheduled coronary angiography at St. John's on 10/07/2026.


Continue cardiovascular risk-factor management and follow up after angiography.


Procedure Summary
Roberto Morales Sandoval is a 68-year-old man undergoing pre-procedure evaluation prior to diagnostic coronary angiography. He has multiple cardiovascular risk factors including diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity, and a remote history of tobacco use.
Prior coronary CT evaluation demonstrated a markedly elevated coronary calcium score of approximately 992, placing him at approximately the 83rd percentile for his age. Stress echocardiography subsequently demonstrated preserved LV systolic function but an abnormal exercise ECG response with 1-1.5 mm ST-T changes. There was no echocardiographic evidence of inducible ischemia at the achieved workload, and his Duke treadmill score was 0, consistent with moderate risk.
Despite the absence of current anginal symptoms, the combination of extensive coronary calcification, abnormal exercise ECG findings, and multiple major cardiovascular risk factors was considered sufficiently high risk to warrant invasive coronary angiography for definitive assessment of coronary anatomy. 
Detailed Procedure
The patient's cardiovascular history and available diagnostic studies were reviewed in preparation for invasive coronary evaluation.
He has significant cardiovascular risk factors including type 2 diabetes mellitus, essential hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity, and previous tobacco exposure. He reports having stopped smoking approximately 24 years ago.
Coronary CT evaluation demonstrated a coronary calcium score of approximately 992, reported at the 83rd percentile for his age, indicating a substantial burden of coronary atherosclerosis.
Stress echocardiography performed 08/19/2026 demonstrated normal LV systolic function with EF 55-60%. The patient exercised for 5 minutes 27 seconds using the standard Bruce protocol and achieved a maximum heart rate of 148 bpm, corresponding to 97% of predicted maximal heart rate. The exercise ECG demonstrated 1-1.5 mm ST-T wave changes. No 2D echocardiographic evidence of inducible ischemia was identified at the achieved workload. Duke treadmill score was 0, placing him in the moderate-risk category.
At the current follow-up, he denies chest pain, dyspnea, or unusual fatigue. Nevertheless, because of the markedly elevated coronary calcium burden, abnormal exercise ECG findings, and significant cardiovascular risk profile, invasive coronary angiography has been recommended for definitive evaluation of coronary anatomy.
Diagnostic coronary angiography is scheduled at St. John's on 10/07/2026. The documented plan is for wrist/radial access. 
Impression


Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease/high coronary atherosclerotic burden. (ICD-10: I25.10)


Markedly elevated coronary calcium score, approximately 992.


Abnormal exercise ECG with 1-1.5 mm ST-T changes.


Preserved LV systolic function, LVEF 55-60%.


Type 2 diabetes mellitus. (ICD-10: E11.9)


Essential hypertension. (ICD-10: I10)


Hyperlipidemia. (ICD-10: E78.5)


Obesity. (ICD-10: E66.9)


Former tobacco use. (ICD-10: Z87.891)


Planned diagnostic coronary angiography for definitive coronary anatomical assessment.

TAN OHA - Pre-Procedure History & Physical
Salient Features
Clinical Profile


70-year-old man with severe aortic stenosis, coronary artery disease with prior coronary stent placement, congestive heart failure, right and left heart failure, diabetes mellitus, hyperlipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea, asthma, and longstanding Parkinson disease.


Presents with chest pain, dyspnea, generalized edema, rapid weight gain, pedal/ankle edema, abdominal fullness, and symptoms consistent with significant volume overload.


Echocardiogram 05/01/2026 demonstrated mildly impaired LV systolic function with LVEF 45-50% and severe aortic stenosis with peak/mean gradients 62.59/40.95 mmHg and calculated aortic valve area 0.6 cm².


Mild mitral regurgitation and elevated RVSP of approximately 44 mmHg were also documented.


Stress echocardiogram 03/11/2025 demonstrated severe aortic stenosis with AVA 0.7 cm², limited exercise capacity, ischemic 2-mm ST-T depression, and failure of the apical lateral wall to augment normally with stress.


Known CAD with prior angiography and coronary stent placement; history documents two coronary stents.


Combined right and left heart catheterization previously performed 05/14/2025.


Current symptoms and severe symptomatic aortic stenosis prompted initiation of TAVR evaluation, including coronary/CT angiographic evaluation at St. John's and referral to the valvular heart team and cardiac surgery.


Significant procedural anxiety/claustrophobia and Parkinsonism are relevant considerations for procedural planning. 


Procedure


Planned angiographic evaluation as part of TAVR workup for severe symptomatic aortic stenosis with known coronary artery disease.


Available documentation specifically orders a coronary CT angiogram for TAVR evaluation at St. John's; an invasive coronary angiogram is not explicitly ordered in the supplied encounter.


Disposition


Proceed with planned angiographic/TAVR evaluation at St. John's according to the valvular heart disease pathway.


Continue outpatient evaluation with the valvular heart disease specialist and cardiac surgeon.


Continue monitoring volume status and response to diuretic therapy.


Procedure Summary
Tanny O'Haley is a 70-year-old man undergoing pre-procedure evaluation in the setting of severe symptomatic aortic stenosis and known coronary artery disease. He has developed significant dyspnea, chest pain, rapid weight gain, peripheral edema, abdominal fullness, and clinical evidence of volume overload/right and left heart failure.
Echocardiography on 05/01/2026 demonstrated severe aortic stenosis with peak/mean transvalvular gradients of 62.59/40.95 mmHg and calculated aortic valve area of 0.6 cm². LV systolic function was mildly impaired with an LVEF of 45-50%. Mild mitral regurgitation and elevated RV systolic pressure of approximately 44 mmHg were also present.
He additionally has established coronary artery disease with prior coronary stent placement. Given symptomatic severe aortic stenosis, heart failure manifestations, chest pain, and known CAD, he is undergoing angiographic and structural heart evaluation as part of the planned TAVR workup. 
Detailed Procedure
The patient's cardiovascular history and available diagnostic studies were reviewed in preparation for angiographic/TAVR evaluation.
He has severe aortic stenosis documented on serial cardiac imaging. Stress echocardiography from 03/11/2025 demonstrated an aortic valve peak/mean gradient of 62.97/45.45 mmHg with calculated AVA of 0.7 cm². Exercise capacity was limited to 2 minutes 35 seconds on the Bruce protocol, reaching 71% of predicted maximal heart rate. The exercise ECG demonstrated ischemic 2-mm ST-T depression, and the apical lateral wall did not demonstrate appropriate augmentation.
Repeat echocardiography on 05/01/2026 confirmed progression/persistence of severe aortic stenosis, with a calculated AVA of 0.6 cm² and peak/mean gradients of 62.59/40.95 mmHg. LVEF was mildly reduced at 45-50%. Mild mitral regurgitation and RVSP of 44.31 mmHg were documented.
Clinically, the patient reports chest pain, dyspnea, rapid weight gain, significant lower-extremity edema, and abdominal/genital swelling consistent with substantial volume overload. Diuretic therapy with furosemide has been intensified.
He also has established coronary artery disease with prior coronary angiography and coronary stent placement. A previous combined right and left heart catheterization is documented from 05/14/2025.
Given symptomatic severe aortic stenosis with heart failure manifestations and underlying coronary disease, further angiographic assessment has been ordered as part of TAVR evaluation. The supplied cardiology plan specifically documents coronary CT angiography at St. John's, together with evaluation by a valvular heart disease specialist and cardiac surgeon. 
Impression


Severe symptomatic aortic stenosis with AVA 0.6 cm² and peak/mean gradients 62.59/40.95 mmHg. (ICD-10: I35.0)


Congestive heart failure with significant volume overload. (ICD-10: I50.9)


Coronary artery disease with prior coronary stent placement. (ICD-10: I25.10)


Acute/recurrent chest pain. (ICD-10: R07.9)


Dyspnea. (ICD-10: R06.00)


Mildly reduced LV systolic function, LVEF 45-50%.


Generalized edema with rapid weight gain. (ICD-10: R60.1)


Parkinson disease.


Obstructive sleep apnea.


Diabetes mellitus and hyperlipidemia.


Planned angiographic evaluation as part of TAVR workup.
